newsitem.title: UK: Horlick ends meeting with lawyer, action undecided.
newsitem.headline: Horlick ends meeting with lawyer, action undecided.

text.p: Former Morgan Grenfell fund manager Nicola Horlick emerged from a marathon meeting with her lawyer on Monday and told reporters that no course of action had yet been decided.

"These things take time," Horlick, who resigned from the Deutsche Bank unit in a blaze of publicity last week, said. "One has to explore all the posibilities. This is not about money, it's about reputation."

Earlier, her lawyer said she wanted an amicable settlement with her ex-employer but that the 35-year-old mother-of-five, one of the most prominent fund managers in London, was prepared to sue if they could not strike a deal.

Horlick resigned last week after Morgan Grenfell Asset Management suspended her amid allegations that she had tried to strike a deal with a rival firm which would have led to Horlick and several of her senior colleagues leaving.

On Friday, Horlick tried to go over the heads of her former bosses at MGAM, taking her fight direct to Deutsche Bank headquarters in Frankfurt. "Frankfurt listened to what I had to say, I'm still convinced that what I'm saying is true, I wasn't about to lead anyone astray," Horlick said after leaving her lawyer's office.

Asked what advice she would give to others faced with a similar situation, Horlick replied: "Fight." She added that her lawyers at legal firm Herbert Smith had been in contact with lawyers representing Morgan Grenfell but a spokesman for the bank was unable to confirm this.
